rule: When implementing Kerberos auth resolution in a Spark provider hook, include the krb5ccache path alongside keytab/principal so REST calls to a Kerberized YARN RM always carry an Authorization header.
trigger: A method returns auth object based on `keytab` and `principal` connection fields but omits a branch for `_use_krb5ccache` or equivalent ccache flag.
rationale: Without the ccache branch, `resolved_yarn_rm_auth` returns None for ccache users; the RM on a Kerberized cluster responds with 401 and polling fails.

evidence.excerpt: REST calls to the RM go out with no Authorization header

rule: Do not add module-level private constants to a provider module unless they are referenced in that module; dead constants must be wired in or removed.
trigger: A new `_SOME_CONF = "..."` constant is introduced at module level in a provider file but has no call-site reference within the same diff.
rationale: An unreferenced constant implies configurable behaviour that is not actually wired in, misleading future contributors about what is and isn't controlled.

evidence.excerpt: `_K8S_DELETE_ON_TERMINATION_CONF` isn't referenced anywhere. Either wire it in or drop it.

rule: Failures in Kubernetes driver-pod deletion must not propagate as task errors; wrap `_delete_driver_pod()` calls with `contextlib.suppress` or a flag that downgrades the error to a warning.
trigger: A call to `_delete_driver_pod()` or equivalent pod-cleanup method appears inline in a polling loop without error suppression or a configurable error-vs-warning flag.
rationale: An unexpected exception during pod deletion forces a full job retry rather than treating deletion as a best-effort cleanup step.

evidence.excerpt: unexpected exception when deleting driver pod forces retry of the whole job

rule: Do not change the default value of an existing operator or hook parameter that affects pre-existing code paths; new code paths may enforce their own floor via `max()` but the legacy default must stay unchanged.
trigger: A diff changes the default of an `__init__` parameter (e.g. `status_poll_interval`) that was already used by a pre-existing execution path, not only by the newly introduced path.
rationale: Changing a shared default silently degrades existing users (e.g. short-running YARN jobs now wait 10 s instead of 1 s) with no opt-out.

evidence.excerpt: the default for the pre-existing codepath should stay at 1

rule: When calling the Spark Standalone REST submission API, check the `success` field before accessing `driverState`; raise with the response's `message` field on failure.
trigger: Code accesses `response.json()["driverState"]` from a Spark Standalone REST response without first asserting `response.json()["success"] is True`.
rationale: When the submission ID is unrecognised, the master is in recovery, or an auth proxy intercepts, `success` is False and `driverState` may be missing or stale, causing KeyError or silent misreporting.

evidence.excerpt: success: false with driverState missing or stale — KeyError or stale value

rule: Do not land unreachable code branches in a PR; either drop scaffolding branches or mark them with a TODO referencing the specific follow-up PR that will make them reachable.
trigger: A diff introduces `if self._hook._is_yarn:` or similar runtime-gated branches that are never reachable from any entry-point added in the same PR.
rationale: Unreachable branches force reviewers to verify code that can never execute, increasing review burden and risk of accepting incorrect logic.

evidence.excerpt: Reads as live branches a reviewer must verify, but they can never execute.

rule: Spark provider REST calls must derive scheme (http/https) and port from Airflow connection extras rather than hardcoding `http://` and a fixed port number.
trigger: A diff introduces a `requests.get(f"http://{host}:<hardcoded_port>/...")` call inside a Spark provider operator or hook.
rationale: Enterprise deployments use TLS and configurable ports (`spark.master.rest.port`); hardcoded values prevent use on those clusters.

evidence.excerpt: enterprise deployments with TLS can't use this path; read scheme from connection extras

rule: Transient HTTP calls inside provider status-polling loops must be wrapped with a retry strategy (e.g. `tenacity`) to avoid burning a task retry slot on a one-second network blip.
trigger: A `requests.get(...)` or similar HTTP call appears inside a polling loop (e.g. inside `get_job_status`, `poll_until_complete`) with no retry/backoff wrapper.
rationale: A transient network error during a status-check raises out of the polling method, falls through executor error handling, and consumes a Airflow task retry slot unnecessarily.

evidence.excerpt: a one-second network blip will burn a retry slot

rule: Provider changelogs must not include a release entry when only test files or non-functional pyproject.toml marker comments were modified in the PR.
trigger: A diff to a provider's `docs/changelog.rst` adds a new version section for a PR whose only changed files are under `tests/` or contain only `# use next version` comments in `pyproject.toml`.
rationale: The release tool may incorrectly flag a PR as a candidate for release; spurious changelog entries must be removed from the release plan.

evidence.excerpt: PR modifies only test file; provider should not have been a release candidate

rule: CLI commands in providers must raise `SystemExit` (not `AirflowConfigException`) for user-facing configuration errors, consistent with other CLI argument validation.
trigger: A `raise AirflowConfigException(...)` or `raise AirflowException(...)` appears inside a CLI command function (functions decorated or called from `airflow/cli/` or provider `cli/` modules).
rationale: Raising a non-SystemExit exception prints a stack trace, which is confusing to users; other CLI argument errors use SystemExit for a clean error message.

evidence.excerpt: raise SystemExit so we are aligned with other SystemExit exceptions for missing arguments

rule: ImportError compatibility shims for Task SDK symbols must carry a `>=X.Y.Z` version marker in a comment, referencing the minimum SDK/Airflow release that introduced the symbol.
trigger: A `try: from airflow.sdk... except ImportError: Symbol = None` block is added without a comment specifying the minimum version that exports the symbol.
rationale: Without a version marker, reviewers cannot determine when the shim can be removed and cannot schedule the deprecation correctly.

evidence.excerpt: the marker can be for >=3.1.9

rule: When a broad `except Exception` handler wraps code that deliberately raises `AirflowException`, re-raise `AirflowException` unchanged before the generic handler to preserve the intended error message.
trigger: A diff introduces a specific `raise AirflowException(...)` inside a `try` block that also has a downstream `except Exception as e` that re-wraps or swallows the exception.
rationale: The broad handler defeats the specific, user-readable error message and will also break tests that assert on the specific message.

evidence.excerpt: broad except re-wraps as unknown Celery SSL Error, defeating the clearer error

rule: Prose notes and warnings in provider changelog RST files must use the RST `.. note::` or `.. warning::` directive, not plain prose, so they render correctly in the documentation site.
trigger: A provider `docs/changelog.rst` diff adds a paragraph that reads as a note or warning without a leading `.. note::` or `.. warning::` RST directive.
rationale: Plain prose in a changelog is not rendered as a callout block; the note/warning styling is lost in the generated docs.

evidence.excerpt: should be under note/warning notion otherwise it won't render nicely

rule: Documentation claims about KubernetesPodOperator deduplication or ambiguity prevention must be scoped to the specific code path (e.g. `get_or_create_pod`) where the guarantee holds, not asserted end-to-end.
trigger: A diff to a provider `docs/` RST file claims "no possibility of ambiguity failure" or equivalent absolute language for pod reconnect behaviour.
rationale: `execute_sync` still calls `find_pod` unconditionally after reconnect, which raises `FoundMoreThanOnePodFailure` for duplicate orphan pods; the absolute claim is false.

evidence.excerpt: execute_sync still calls find_pod unconditionally; ambiguity failure can still occur

rule: New parameters added to `KubernetesPodOperator.__init__` must have a matching docstring entry describing the parameter type; for `Callable` parameters the docstring must name each positional argument's meaning.
trigger: A diff adds a new keyword argument to `KubernetesPodOperator.__init__` (or any `*Operator.__init__` in the cncf.kubernetes provider) without a corresponding `:param name:` entry in the class docstring.
rationale: Users and IDE tooling rely on operator docstrings for parameter discovery; omitting entries for Callable parameters leaves the expected signature undocumented.

evidence.excerpt: docstring of container_name_log_prefix_enabled and log_formatter is missing

rule: XCom push guards in KubernetesPodOperator must use `if value is not None` rather than `if value` (or `if not value`) so that falsy values such as `0`, `False`, or empty string are persisted correctly.
trigger: A diff introduces `if not value:` or `if value:` as a guard before an XCom push call inside `KubernetesPodOperator` (or its mixins).
rationale: A falsy value like `0` or `False` would silently not be pushed; downstream tasks that rely on the XCom receive nothing instead of the actual result.

evidence.excerpt: if value evaluates to False would not persist; change to explicit NULL check

rule: When persisting pod identity to the task state store, either verify the stored `uid` against the live pod on reconnect or omit `uid` from the stored payload so the schema does not imply verification that is not performed.
trigger: A diff stores `uid` alongside `name`/`namespace` in a task-state-store payload for pod identity, but the reconnect code only uses `name`/`namespace` without comparing `pod.metadata.uid` to the stored uid.
rationale: A stored uid that is never checked is dead weight that misleads readers into thinking pod identity is verified; tests that store a uid without asserting on it expose the same gap.

evidence.excerpt: persisted uid is currently dead weight; schema implies a check that isn't performed

rule: When a parameter's behaviour is gated on a minimum Airflow version, its docstring must state the version constraint explicitly (e.g. "Only available for Airflow 3.3+").
trigger: A new operator parameter is introduced whose full behaviour requires Airflow ≥X.Y but the `:param name:` docstring entry omits the version constraint.
rationale: Users on older Airflow versions will enable the parameter expecting full behaviour; the constraint must be documented at the parameter level to prevent silent degradation.

evidence.excerpt: Only available for Airflow 3.3+

rule: When replacing a deprecated parameter with a new version-gated one, silently translate the deprecated parameter's value for users below the minimum required version rather than forcing them to change parameter names.
trigger: A diff deprecates parameter A and introduces replacement parameter B that only works on Airflow ≥X.Y, without fallback logic that makes B behave like A when the runtime version is below X.Y.
rationale: Users below the minimum version should get the old behaviour transparently; forcing a parameter rename without a fallback is a breaking change for older deployments.

evidence.excerpt: handle durable for Airflow<3.3; make it work as reattach_on_restart under the hood

rule: Kubernetes field selectors using comma-separated `!=` expressions must be verified to produce the correct Boolean semantics (`NOT A AND NOT B`, not `NOT (A OR B)`) before merging.
trigger: A diff introduces a Kubernetes field selector string of the form `status.phase!=X,status.phase!=Y` where the intent is to exclude pods in either state X or state Y.
rationale: The comma is logical AND: `status.phase!=X,status.phase!=Y` means NOT X AND NOT Y. If the intent is NOT (X OR Y) the logic is correct, but authors frequently misread it and the reviewer requires an explicit local-cluster verification.

evidence.excerpt: NOT RUNNING AND NOT PENDING when I test the field selector locally
